Reasons for tracking refrigerants. Because of the wide variety of refrigerant applications and classifications, it is important to develop a refrigerant management plan to track locations, types, and quantities of refrigerants throughout a facility or a portfolio of facilities. Building owners track refrigerants for several reasons, including: • Reducing cost and optimizing performance. Each piece of equipment is designed to use a specific amount of refrigerant. The amount of refrigerant is also referred to as the refrigerant charge. The refrigerant is at a different pressure than the air around the unit; therefore, it is prone to leak through worn seals, poor piping joints, and valves. Without the correct charge, the equipment will not operate at the rated efficiency, which can increase operational costs and shorten equipment lifetimes. There is also cost associated with adding the lost refrigerant, including both the service to replace and the expense of purchasing the added refrigerant. • Mitigating risk. Tracking the quantity of refrigerants currently in use and the anticipated lifetimes of equipment using them will help reduce risk related to increased maintenance and operational costs of refrigerant leakage. Some refrigerants are blends that contain different refrigerants. When they leak, the different refrigerants leak at different rates. Just adding the original refrigerant may or may not be effective, resulting in more repair costs. A refrigerant management plan can help track equipment issues and allow owners to be proactive to avoid costly repairs, equipment replacement, and, in some cases, local compliance issues, including refrigerant disposal. • Complying with protocols.
